title: Jobs and steps
summary: A job runs a list of steps on a runner. Steps in one job run in order and share that job's working environment.
introduction: A job runs a list of steps on a runner. Steps in one job run in order and share that job's working environment. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A job runs a list of steps on a runner. Steps in one job run in order and share that job's working environment.

blocks.code:
jobs:
  explain:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: First step
        run: echo "Read"
      - name: Second step
        run: echo "Check"
blocks.title: Jobs and steps

blocks.text: The job prints Read before Check. Separate jobs do not automatically share the same filesystem.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Add a third step named Finish.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not assume a file from one job appears in another job automatically.
For more detail later, use this [GitHub Actions further reading](https://docs.github.com/en/actions).

seo.title: GitHub Actions: Jobs and steps
seo.description: Learn about jobs and steps in GitHub Actions. Follow a small example, understand the result, and practise with a clear question.
